stories.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
stories.summary: Police discovered three bodies at a suspect's home after a deadly shooting spree in central Krakow. The attacker reportedly fired at random crowds from his car, leaving six victims dead. Officers halted the rampage within minutes, arresting the heavily armed man after an exchange of gunfire.
stories.why_it_matters: Poland is grappling with a rare, deadly mass attack linked to far-right extremism.
stories.uncertainty: Authorities have not yet released the suspect's name or confirmed how he obtained the weapons.
stories.background: Krakow is Poland's second-largest city, centered around a historic medieval square popular with visitors. Mass shootings and acts of domestic terrorism have historically been very rare across the country.

jargon.meaning: Someone with an extreme devotion to their nation, often expressing hostility toward foreign groups.

stories.title: Briton among six dead after gunman opens fire in Kraków market square
stories.summary: Police discovered three slain relatives at a suspect's home following a deadly shooting in Poland. The heavily armed gunman fired on crowds in Kraków's busy central square before officers arrested him. Officials labeled the rampage, which left several dead, an act of terror tied to far-right extremism.
stories.why_it_matters: This rare mass attack has shaken Poland and raised urgent concerns over public safety and extremism.
stories.uncertainty: Authorities have not yet confirmed the identities of two victims or how many people suffered gunshot wounds.
stories.background: Kraków's central square is a famous historic destination that attracts millions of international travelers each year. While public mass shootings are historically rare in Poland, the nation has seen growing numbers of legal firearms.

jargon.meaning: Extreme devotion to one's nation, often accompanied by hostility toward outside groups or minorities.

stories.title: Can the Zelda remake capture the magic of the original?
stories.summary: Playtesters found a spooky room in the new Legend of Zelda remake too scary, forcing developers to adjust it. Nintendo kept the gameplay faithful to the N64 original while modernizing controls and updating graphics. Developers also redesigned famously difficult dungeons to make them easier for players.
stories.why_it_matters: Nintendo modernized one of gaming's most celebrated classics while trying not to lose its original charm.
stories.uncertainty: It remains unconfirmed whether players will feel Nintendo played it too safe by keeping gameplay so similar.
stories.background: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time originally launched on the Nintendo 64 and pioneered standard 3D gaming features. Video game remakes rebuild older titles using modern graphics and updated control schemes.

jargon.meaning: A self-contained area in a video game packed with puzzles, enemies, and obstacles to navigate.
A feature that automatically keeps your character's view and attacks focused on a specific enemy.

stories.title: Traders 'priced out' of £12,000 Christmas market pitches
stories.summary: Local traders say surging stall fees of up to £15,000 are pricing them out of Liverpool's Christmas market. A new private operator recently took over running the festive event. Small business owners warn these high costs will prevent local sellers from participating this year.
stories.why_it_matters: skyrocketing stall fees may keep local independent craftspeople out of major holiday markets.
stories.uncertainty: The council was unable to specify how many local traders have signed up for the market.
stories.background: Cities often hire outside companies to manage seasonal public attractions like holiday markets. These event operators set vendor stall fees, while local governments sometimes receive a share of the income.

jargon.meaning: The cost to rent a stall space at a market or public event.
A process where businesses submit bids to win a contract to run a service.

stories.title: Can Congress fix affordability? MIT's Daron Acemoglu weighs in
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence could become a major factor in how lawmakers tackle everyday affordability issues. NPR host Scott Simon interviewed MIT economics professor Daron Acemoglu on the topic. They explored potential actions the incoming Democratic majority in Congress might take to help consumers.
stories.why_it_matters: Congress may look at technology like artificial intelligence to help address high living costs.
stories.uncertainty: The text does not specify what specific policies Congress might use or how AI helps.
stories.background: Affordability describes how manageable everyday expenses are for regular household budgets. Economists and lawmakers frequently explore how new technology can help bring down living costs.

jargon.meaning: How easy or difficult it is for average people to pay for basic living expenses.

stories.title: Accused charity-fraud couple survive first night in remand prison
stories.summary: A former beauty queen and her husband spent their first night in prison following fraud charges. Authorities reportedly stated that the couple adjusted well to their new surroundings behind bars. They face public fraud accusations involving misused donation funds from her Goodness Foundation.
stories.why_it_matters: High-profile figures face legal trouble when charity funds are allegedly misused.
stories.uncertainty: It remains unclear how much money was allegedly taken or when trial proceedings will begin.
stories.background: Charity foundations rely on public trust to raise funds for good causes. When leadership is accused of financial wrongdoing, legal authorities step in to investigate and hold suspects during court proceedings.

jargon.meaning: A detention facility where accused individuals are kept while waiting for trial.
Deceiving members of the public to unlawfully obtain money or benefits.
